title: Align Story 21.12 AC3 and Story 21.10 assertions in epic_21_multi_account_test.dart with the UI-level claims their names/comments make
rule: TQ-8 (weak assertion narrower than the AC title)

evidence.quote: test('AC3: cloud-born account does not show upgrade option', () {

why: Story 21.12's AC3 test name promises 'does not show upgrade option' (a UI/screen claim) but only asserts `cloudState.isLocalBorn == false`, which is a one-line freezed getter (`tier == Tier.localBorn` in auth_state.dart:77) -- it never touches whatever widget actually gates the upgrade button, so a regression in that gating logic would not be caught here despite the AC's name. Story 21.10 similarly comments '// → picker' / '// → welcome' next to plain registry-count assertions without ever exercising the routing decision. Unlike the DEC-34 group a few hundred lines below in the same file, which explicitly documents 'the UI enforcement is covered by code review of account_picker_screen.dart:_activateLocalAccountFromLocalData', neither of these tests says where -- or whether -- the claimed UI behavior is actually verified elsewhere.
recommendation: Either rename the tests to describe what they actually check (data-layer state, not UI), add the missing UI/routing assertion, or add a DEC-34-style comment pointing to where the UI-level behavior is verified.
acceptance_criteria: Story 21.12 AC3's test name matches its assertion scope, or it exercises the actual upgrade-option gating logic
Story 21.10's picker/welcome comments are backed by an assertion or a pointer comment naming where routing is verified
